messages.content: Write the introduction to a public product roadmap for a developer tools company. Around 200 words.

output:
Roughly 205 words. It passes the slopwatch gate clean.

## Our roadmap

This page is the same roadmap we use internally, with the customer names taken out. We publish it because the alternative — you finding out what we built after we built it — has cost us too many good conversations.

Three things shape what is on here. First, the support queue. If forty people write in about the same rough edge in a month, that edge gets a card, and we say so on the card. Second, the parts of the product we know are held together with tape: the CLI's config loader, the way builds retry, the parts we would be embarrassed to demo. Those rarely come from customer requests, so we schedule them ourselves. Third, a small budget for work nobody asked for, because a few of our best features started that way and we would like to keep the door open.

Dates are quarters, not days, and quarters slip. When something slips we move the card and write one line about why. When we kill something we leave the card up with a note instead of deleting it.

If a card is wrong, or missing, the issue tracker is open and we read it.

The specifics (support-queue threshold, the CLI examples, quarterly granularity) are placeholders — swap in your own so the concreteness is真 rather than decorative.
